items.title: The Switch in dark: a lit off track, a light thumb, a per-switch checked ink
items.evidence: Thumb: switch/styles.css:36-37 paints `--card` with `--shadow-md`. The dark `--card` is hsl(26 22% 17%) (tokens/dark-arm.css:99), so the dark thumb is the card's own colour. Off face in dark: control-bit.css:192-194 sets `--control-bit-fill: oklch(0 0 0 / 0.14)`. That recess is deliberate (the rule is written at control-bit.css:166-191) and Checkbox and Radio share it. Checked face: control-bit.css:203-206 reads `--control-checked-bg` at the element; the token is defined once, at tokens/scale-paper.css:84, and glass never sets it on a control. A value set on one Switch's class therefore tints that Switch alone, and its disabled-checked arm follows (control-bit.css:240-254). A second name for the same value is what scale-paper.css:13-16 forbids. Precedent for lifting in dark: the dock seats' dark arm lifts toward the foreground (tokens/dark-arm.css:294-301). release/11.1.1 changes neither switch/ nor control-bit.css (git diff master release/11.1.1). No booked row covers the Switch's dark look; O-360 is about the Slider's thumb in light.
items.row: LF-28 (hassio round 13, H5). In dark the Switch is a dark knob in a dark groove: the thumb paints the card colour, and the shared recess darkens the off track under it. The owner told hassio "the toggle is too dark" (R11 Q-023). hassio keeps its local colours until he picks between them and the library's. Reading: the off track's recess and the card-coloured thumb are both deliberate defaults, so the new look is the owner's call, and it ships in a minor. Default offered to him: a light thumb in both schemes, lifted toward the foreground in dark as the dock seats are, keeping the library's edge; in dark, an off track a step lighter than the card, on the Switch only, so the Checkbox and Radio keep their recess. Per-switch ink needs no new name: `--control-checked-bg` set on one Switch already tints only that switch, and the README will say so. The disabled face is LF-25 (11.1.2). Lands in 11.3.0 once the owner picks.
items.reply: The dark Switch's look is the owner's call. We'll show him a light thumb and a lit off track in dark beside today's Switch, and ship the one he picks in 11.3.0. You can already give one switch its own checked colour by setting `--control-checked-bg` on that Switch; it tints only that switch, and the README will say so. The disabled face comes sooner, in 11.1.2 (LF-25).

items.title: An unchecked disabled Switch looks like an enabled one
items.evidence: control-bit.css:226-238: the disabled arm softens `--control-bit-mark-ink` and `--control-bit-edge` to 45 % and sets `cursor: not-allowed`. On a Switch the mark is the thumb (Switch.vue:49-52). The thumb paints `--card` with `--shadow-md` (switch/styles.css:36-37) and never reads `--control-bit-mark-ink`; only `.control-bit__mark` reads that (control-bit.css:353). The unchecked face fill is untouched as well (control-bit.css:109, and :193 in dark). No other stylesheet in src styles a disabled Switch. So an unchecked disabled Switch differs from an enabled one only by its 1 px edge. The register's own note (control-bit.css:213-222) names exactly this as the defect it set out to cure. A checked disabled Switch does recede (control-bit.css:240-254). An unchecked Checkbox is mostly edge, so its 45 % edge shows more; measure it in the same cell. Unchanged on release/11.1.1.
items.row: LF-25 (hassio round 12, U7; folded into LF-28). With both switches off, a read-only Switch and a live one differ only by a slightly softer 1 px rim, in both schemes, at 390 and 1440. Confirmed in source. The disabled arm softens the mark ink and the edge, but a Switch's mark is its thumb, which paints the card colour with a shadow and never reads the mark ink, and the off fill does not change either. The register's own rule is that disabled is ink, not opacity, and must be visible, so this is a defect. Cure in 11.1.2: on a disabled Switch the thumb's plate and shadow, and the face's fill, recede with the ink; the box and the seat stay as they are. Witness: an off disabled Switch beside an off enabled one in both schemes, with a measured difference against v11.1.0, and the same cell for an unchecked Checkbox. Until then hassio shows read-only rules as words, with no shim.
items.reply: Fixed in 11.1.2: a disabled Switch's thumb and track fade with it, so an off read-only switch reads as disabled next to a live one in both schemes. We'll check the unchecked Checkbox in the same pass.

items.title: A thumb that reads raised over a coloured fill in dark, and one thumb ink in every scope
items.dedupe_of: Related, not duplicates: O-408 (the Slider's thumbless form), O-360 (the Slider thumb's default in light, an owner question), LF-28 (the Switch's thumb), LF-5 in O-377a (the slide control)
items.evidence: Capsule: glass-capsule.css:35-56 fills from the floating veil through `--glass-capsule-fill`, so over a saturated fill it reads as a darker disc of that fill. Opaque rung: surface-axis.css:81-89 paints solid `--card`, which in dark is hsl(26 22% 17%) (tokens/dark-arm.css:99). Switch thumb: switch/styles.css:36-37 (`--card`, `--shadow-md`). Slider thumb: slider/styles.css:248-254 (`--slider-thumb-bg`, default `--foreground`, over `--shadow-sm`). The dark lift the ask cites: tokens/dark-arm.css:294-301. Scope split: inside `@supports (color: contrast-color(white))` (ladder.css:254), ladder.css:269-280 re-points `color`, `--foreground` and `--muted-foreground` to `contrast-color(var(--card))` on every glass rung under `@container style(--glass-backdrop: light)`, and `.glass-floating` and `.glass-overlay` set that value (ladder.css:131, :150). So a thumb in a `.glass-wash` row inside a sheet takes the flipped ink, while a rail placed directly in the sheet does not. That is the flip working as designed, not a fault in the slider: the same rule turns the row's words to the same pure ink, so the thumb matches its own row. The slider's stated reason for using the foreground, that it is the one tone apart from the fill and the track (slider/styles.css:240-244), still holds in that scope, because the dark fill ink reads `--foreground` too (:165) and moves with it. A thumb exempt from the flip needs an ink the flip does not re-point, which is the declared thumb ink of (a): a new token and a look. release/11.1.1 changes the slider only under reduced motion (slider/styles.css:603-623 there). Booked nearby: O-408 (no visible Slider thumb, a minor), O-360 (the Slider thumb's default in light, an owner question), LF-5 in O-377a (a slide control, 11.3.0).
items.row: LF-18 (hassio round 12, U3 and U4). (a) The library's three thumbs handle a thumb on a fill three ways, and none reads raised in both schemes. The capsule darkens what it sits on; the opaque rung and the Switch thumb are the dark card in dark; the Slider thumb is the foreground. The ask is one declared thumb rung, lifted toward the foreground in dark as the dock seats are, read by the Switch, the Slider and a capsule. Reading: a new token plus a dark look, so 11.3.0, with the owner's pick on LF-28 setting the dark value. It lands with LF-5's slide control, which hassio's lock slide needs. (b) The Slider thumb takes two inks depending on scope: a rail in a row inside a sheet draws pure black or white beside the sheet's own softer rail. The cause is the ladder's deliberate contrast flip, which re-points the foreground for everything in a nested glass rung, the row's words included, so the thumb matches its row. Exempting the thumb is a choice of look and needs (a)'s declared ink, so (b) joins (a) in 11.3.0, with the witness that two rails in one sheet, one in a row and one on the sheet, draw one thumb ink in both schemes. Both halves follow O-408, the owner's thumbless capped Slider, which may leave no Slider thumb to paint.
items.reply: A single thumb colour that reads raised over a coloured fill in both schemes, and stays the same wherever the thumb is drawn, including a row inside a sheet, comes in 11.3.0 with the slide control you asked for in LF-5. Its dark value follows the owner's choice for the Switch. The Slider's own thumb follows his new thumbless Slider design.

items.title: A choice's chosen and asked forms, and a disabled icon-only button
items.evidence: (1) toggle-group/styles.css:117-121 at master: a chosen item gets a 12 % foreground fill, the full foreground ink and weight 600. release/11.1.1 drops the weight (cc13da049, styles.css:119-122 there), so every chosen item now shows by ink and a 12 % fill alone. The sheet's own note says fill alone cannot make the distinction (toggle-group/styles.css:101-103). The ink register's rule is that where fill carries a state alone, it must read 3:1 against the unselected sibling (tokens/color-radius.css:149-155). On an icon-only item the ink step on a thin glyph is small, and the weight never reached it on master either, so 11.1.1 changes nothing for icon-only items. (2) ToggleGroupItem.vue:21-26: its props are value, disabled and class. Button's `loading` (Button.vue:57-58) renders the one in-flight mark (:197). DotRing has no barrel (_shared/feedback/README.md:33-35). 11.1.2 already tweens that mark in and out (O-390(i), glass-11.1.1-scope.md:130). (3) button/styles.css:263-276: a disabled Button keeps its plate at full alpha and dims only the ink, a stated choice (:264-271). ToggleGroupItem uses opacity instead (toggle-group/styles.css:127-131), and the binary controls soften ink and edge (control-bit.css:226-238): three disabled grammars in one library.
items.row: LF-19 (hassio round 12, U4). (1) A chosen icon-only ToggleGroup item reads only as a slightly darker disc. On master the chosen weight has no word to reach. 11.1.1 removes the weight from every item, so a chosen word no longer pushes its neighbours, which leaves ink and a 12 % fill, a pair the stylesheet itself says cannot carry the state. Measure a chosen icon-only item against its neighbours on a tinted ground under the 3:1 rule. The stronger chosen form is a look for the owner, built in 11.3.0. (2) `loading` on ToggleGroupItem: the Button's dot ring in the item's glyph or beside its word, `aria-busy` on the item, and the group still reachable by keyboard. A new prop, so 11.3.0; DotRing stays unexported. (3) A disabled icon-only secondary Button keeps a full raised disc with a faint glyph, beside a group of choices that fades as a whole. The rule that keeps a Button's plate at full alpha is deliberate for word buttons. Whether an icon-only Button's plate recedes, and whether the library keeps three disabled grammars, is for the owner to decide. Default offered: on icon-only buttons only, the plate recedes with the glyph, in 11.3.0.
items.reply: In 11.3.0 a ToggleGroup item gets `loading`, with the same dot ring as Button. Two looks go to the owner first: a stronger chosen state for icon-only items, and a disabled icon-only Button whose plate fades with its glyph. 11.1.1 already drops the bold on chosen items, so a chosen word no longer moves its neighbours.

items.title: A single ToggleGroup a keyboard can move across without choosing
items.evidence: ToggleGroup.vue:92-97 fixes `activation` by type: automatic for `single`, manual for `multiple`. Its props (ToggleGroup.vue:42-48) give no way to change it. The engine already does both. Automatic selects on every focus move (tabs/composables/useTabRovingFocus.ts:121-127). Manual moves the tab stop and commits on Enter or Space (:108-114, :198-207); a multiple group takes that path today. SegmentedTabs already publishes the same prop, default automatic (tabs/SegmentedTabs.vue:39, :110). Unchanged on release/11.1.1. No booked row.
items.row: LF-20 (hassio round 12, U5). Home's part of the day and the Schedule's phases are single ToggleGroups whose pick opens a confirm sheet. Automatic activation selects on every arrow key, so each arrow opens the sheet for the next phase. A keyboard user cannot reach the third phase without dismissing a sheet for the second, and a screen reader hears a dialog open on every arrow. Confirmed: ToggleGroup fixes activation by type and offers no prop for it. The selection engine already supports manual activation, and SegmentedTabs exposes it. Cure: an `activation` prop on ToggleGroup (`automatic` or `manual`), defaulting to today's behaviour; under manual, arrows move focus and Space or Enter choose. Additive, a new prop: 11.3.0. Witness: a single group with manual activation emits no model update across three arrow presses, then one update on Enter and one on Space.
items.reply: 11.3.0 adds an `activation` prop to ToggleGroup, the same one SegmentedTabs has. With `manual`, the arrow keys only move focus and Space or Enter choose, so your confirm sheet opens once, on a real pick. Today's behaviour stays the default.

items.title: ToggleGroup items of equal width, and start-aligned items in a vertical group
items.evidence: toggle-group/styles.css:51-61: an item is `flex: none` with `justify-content: center`, so it takes its words' width and centres its content. :41-44: a vertical group stretches each item to full width, but the content stays centred. :22-26: the group is `fit-content` and wraps (:24), so equal widths also need the group to fill its line. Under the ask's `flex: 1 1 0` a wrapped short last line stretches its items wider than those above it (three items wrapping two and one), so equal widths across wrapped lines need equal tracks, not flex growth. release/11.1.1 only drops the chosen weight in this file (cc13da049). Glass's own demo mounts no vertical ToggleGroup (git grep), and no booked row covers this.
items.row: LF-31 (hassio round 13, U1; the owner's Q-056 to hassio). Items take their words' width, so Day and Sleeptime on one line are two widths, and a vertical group centres each item's glyph and words across a full-width item. Two additions in 11.3.0. (1) An equal-width option, as a prop on ToggleGroup: the group fills its line and its items share it equally, on wrapped lines too. (2) Start-aligned content as a value of a new alignment prop. Making start the default for vertical groups would change every consumer's vertical groups, so that is the owner's pick. His Q-056 to hassio, and the fact that a vertical set of options reads as a list, are the reasons to offer it. Horizontal groups are unchanged either way.
items.reply: In 11.3.0 a ToggleGroup can lay out its items at equal widths across the line, and a vertical group can start each item's glyph and words at its start edge. Whether start alignment becomes the default for vertical groups is the owner's call. Horizontal groups keep today's layout unless you turn on equal widths.

items.title: An unpicked ToggleGroup item's words on a tinted light ground
items.evidence: The unpicked item's ink is `--muted-foreground` (toggle-group/styles.css:67), which is `--neutral-5`, hsl(30 22% 40%), #7C6650 (tokens/color-radius.css:45, :91). The token's own comment puts it at 5.21:1 on the library's page, `--neutral-0` (color-radius.css:40, :45). The group paints no ground of its own (toggle-group/styles.css:2-13). On glass's own glass plates the item's ink is already lifted: every glass rung re-points `--muted-foreground` to `--on-glass-muted` (ladder.css:199-209), which in light is hsl(30 26% 35%) at 5.76:1 against its plate (tokens/on-glass-fg.css:35). The ground under 4.5:1 is the dashboard's own: R13-DESIGN.md:463-468 names it as the page's four radial washes (#E5D4BF at their darkest), with 4.67:1 on the dashboard's flat page and 5.01:1 on a card. Glass's own light surfaces are already booked: words on light Dialog, Sheet and menu surfaces to 4.5:1 (O-390(e), glass-11.1.1-scope.md:130), muted ink in light (O-379(e)), and ToggleGroup's off-state text at 4.5:1 (W-R.1 G4, a 12.0.0 wave, waves/W-R.1.md:128, :157).
items.row: LF-34 (hassio round 13, U1; D13). An unpicked item's words read 3.74:1 on the dashboard's light radial washes, 4.67:1 on its flat page and 5.01:1 on a card. The washes are the dashboard's ground, not the library's. Glass's muted ink reads 5.21:1 on the library's light page, and on glass's own glass plates the item already takes the darker on-glass ink. No part can hold 4.5:1 over every ground a site paints. hassio has already moved light to the flat ground (D13), where the ink passes, so no shim is needed. Glass's own light surfaces are covered by booked rows: words to 4.5:1 on the light Dialog, Sheet and menu (O-390(e), 11.1.2), and W-R.1 G4's off-state text rule (12.0.0). Nothing new is booked.
items.reply: No library change here. The words pass on the library's own light page (5.21:1), on a card and on our glass plates; only the dashboard's radial washes take them below 4.5:1, and your flat light ground already fixes that. Words on our light sheets and dialogs reach 4.5:1 in 11.1.2.

items.title: A focus ring at 3:1 on tinted and glass grounds, and a more-contrast ring
items.dedupe_of: O-337 (FOCUS-RING-RECIPE, the focus-ring contrast floor, 11.1.2); related: O-225 (11.1.2 row 5), O-104, O-397
items.evidence: The house ring does not use `--focus-ring-color`. `.focus-ring:focus-visible` draws `--foreground` at `--ink-perimeter` 0.48 (utilities/base.css:144-151; tokens/color-radius.css:147). So does `.interactive-item:focus-visible` (base.css:244-252), and so does the Switch, Checkbox and Radio face (control-bit.css:132-136, :320-327). The source's 3:1 claim (base.css:137-138) is measured on opaque grounds. A 48 % ink over a mid-tone tint, or over a glass sheet in dark, blends toward that ground; O-104 measured 2.15:1 on translucent grounds. `--focus-ring-color` (color-radius.css:174, dark-arm.css:150) is read by `--focus-ring-shadow` (scale-paper.css:40) and by a few parts, for example sheet/styles.css:319 and expandable-container/styles.css:90. Booked for 11.1.2: O-337's floor (INBOUND O-337, FOCUS-RING-RECIPE; glass-11.1.1-scope.md:83): focus rings on the dock and form controls meet 3:1 against their ground. Row 5 (O-225, glass-11.1.1-scope.md:31-36) moves every `--focus-ring-shadow` reader onto this same 48 % outline, so by itself it does not lift the ring on a tinted ground; its witness is every atom's ring at 3:1 in light and dark. O-397 (scope :162) makes the ring follow the control's radius. More contrast: glass already has `prefers-contrast: more` brackets that firm glass plates (glass/a11y-fallback.css:37-47) and draw solid borders on selected and invalid items (styles/accessibility.css:7-29), but none of them touches a focus ring. No ring in src/styles/utilities has such an arm. The ask cites WCAG 2.4.11; in WCAG 2.2 that is Focus Not Obscured, and the 3:1 floor comes from 1.4.11, the bar glass's own source uses (control-bit.css:126).
items.row: LF-39 (hassio round 13, U1; U2 measures the grounds). The ring falls under 3:1 on a dark card, on a lit room card's tinted glass and on a glass sheet in dark, and there is no more-contrast arm. One correction to the ask: the ring is the foreground at 48 % alpha, not `--focus-ring-color`, which is why it fades toward any mid-tone ground. The 3:1 half is the fault already booked as O-337's focus-ring contrast floor in 11.1.2. O-225's row in the same release moves the remaining shadow rings onto this same outline, so it is related but is not the cure. The floor's witness adds a tinted card and a glass sheet in dark to its grounds, with hassio's U2 table as a second witness, and that measurement decides the cure's form: a solid ink or a two-tone ring. The `prefers-contrast: more` ring is new behaviour, not a defect cure, so it goes to 11.3.0, as a focus line in the library's existing more-contrast brackets. If the 11.1.2 cure is already a solid ring, that line adds nothing and the half closes.
items.reply: Focus rings that hold 3:1 against their ground in both schemes are already planned for 11.1.2. We'll add tinted cards and dark glass sheets to the grounds we check, and your U2 measurements will be a useful second check. A stronger ring for when the system asks for more contrast comes in 11.3.0.

items.title: A pressable row part
items.dedupe_of: Related, not a duplicate: O-151 BL-FW14OA50-2 (value.js's list-row primitive, carried by W-J.1's selectable tile, 12.0.0)
items.evidence: `.interactive-item` is defined in utilities/base.css:200-260, not btn.css as the ask says (btn.css:51 only mentions it). Only menu-family rows compose it: _shared/menu/rowClass.ts:28-29, menu/DropdownMenuItem.vue:43, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem.vue:46, DropdownMenuRadioItem.vue:43, DropdownMenuSubTrigger.vue:36. It brings a hover fill (base.css:229-240), a focus outline (:244-252) and a press scale (:253-260), but no touch floor and no ink or layout of its own. On 11.1.1 it keeps its size on a press under reduced motion (8e72e127c, base.css:336-337 there). Button centres its content (button/styles.css:51) and paints the Button's own ink (:41, :44). No row part exists in src/components. Nearest booking: value.js's list-row primitive (INBOUND O-151, BL-FW14OA50-2) went to W-J.1, whose tile is that list row (waves/W-J.1.md:24), a selectable multi-line tile placed in 12.0.0 (waves/INDEX.md:100). It is a choice with radio semantics, not one press that opens something.
items.row: LF-36 (hassio round 13, U1). A row that is one press and opens something has no library part. Examples: a door opening its lock sheet, a count of things not working opening its list, a floor in Devices. `.interactive-item` is a menu-row utility with no touch floor, and a stretched Button centres its words in the Button's ink. hassio uses text with a trailing chevron Button for now. Proposed new part: full width, content at the start, the full foreground ink, an optional trailing glyph, the menu row's hover, press and focus, and the 44 touch floor on a coarse pointer, rendered as a button or a link. 11.3.0. Related, not a duplicate: W-J.1's selectable list-row tile (O-151, 12.0.0) is a choice, not a press-to-open row. The new part takes the same row geometry and corner, so the two do not fork.
items.reply: A pressable row part is planned for 11.3.0: full width, content at the start, full-strength text, an optional trailing glyph, and the library's hover, press and focus at the 44 px touch size. Until then your text with a trailing chevron button is the right stand-in.

items.title: A settings row with its switch at the end, and a name no smaller than its description
items.evidence: LabeledField.vue:121-125: `horizontal` is a grid of `minmax(8rem, 0.382fr) minmax(0, 1fr)`, so the control starts the second column, part way across the row. :127-134 collapse it to stacked below a 36rem viewport, not its container. The only layouts are `default` and `horizontal` (labeled-field/types.ts:6). Type: Label paints `--control-label` (label/Label.vue:96), which is `--control-text` × 0.886653 (tokens/sizing.css:42). `--control-text` is `--type-small` × `--ui-scale` (sizing.css:35), and `--ui-scale` is 1 on a fine pointer (sizing.css:16). The description is `--type-small` (LabeledField.vue:102-107), so on a computer the name is 0.887 of its description; on a coarse pointer (`--ui-coarse-scale` 1.5, sizing.css:20) it is 1.33 times the description. The 0.887 is a ratio to the control's own text (sizing.css:37-42, PROPORTION §1.4) and says nothing of the description, and the README states no rule for it, so no written law is broken. Any cure changes the type of every LabeledField at a fine pointer, which is a changed default and not a patch. Keying LabeledField to its container is W-E.9 (PLAN.md:158), unplaced (waves/INDEX.md:65). Booked beside it for 11.1.2: O-379(a) (the error line's tween) and O-379(e) (the description's muted ink in light, which is ink, not size). Unchanged on release/11.1.1.
items.row: LF-37 (hassio round 13, U1; D5). Settings' four LabeledSwitch rows put the switch at the start of the second column, part way across, never at the row's end. On a computer the name is also smaller than its description: 0.887 of its size. Both land in 11.3.0. (1) The name and description sizes: the label's ratio is tied to the control's text, not to the description, so the inversion breaks no written rule. Curing it changes the type of every field on a computer, which makes it a changed default, so it ships in a minor, not 11.1.2. Default offered: the description takes the label's size, so a field's name is never smaller than its description; on a coarse pointer nothing changes. Witness: the computed sizes at a fine and a coarse pointer. (2) A feature: `layout="row"`, with the name and description at the start and the control at the row's end, on one line while the words fit and stacked below that width, keyed to the field's own width (the row layout carries its own container query; W-E.9 is unplaced). A new layout value.
items.reply: In 11.3.0 LabeledField gets a row layout: name and description at the start, the switch at the row's end, on one line while the words fit. In the same release a field's description stops being larger than its name on a computer.
